== Biography ==
William was born about 1747. He is the son of [[Glasgow-1070|George Glasgow]] and [[Williamson-12853|Agnes Williamson]].

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible William Glascoe, Maryland notice ===
A Lancaster Goal notice dated 13 October says John M’Connel, about 35, imprisoned as a suspected runaway servant, claims to belong to William Glascoe in Maryland, about forty miles from Baltimore.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39392109/ Pennsylvania Gazette, 1775-10-25, p.1].</ref>

The Maryland location is John M’Connel’s attributed claim, not independently proved residence. The notice gives no relatives for William or evidence that he was the 1760 London defendant.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1124]]. The Scottish baptism in 1747 permits adult age in 1775; it does not supply a later Maryland residence.

=== Possible Colinton death and burial, 1824 ===

A Colinton transcript records William Glasgow of Hailes Quarry, aged 76, dying on 16 September 1824 and buried on 19 September. It gives a mortcloth charge of 5/-.<ref name="Colinton1824">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Deaths & Burials 1564–2017'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FLOTHIAN%2FFHS%2FBUR%2F017711 William Glasgow, GBPRS/LOTHIAN/FHS/BUR/017711], Colinton, Midlothian, parish 677, book 6, page 14. Residence Hailes Quarry; age 76; death 16 September 1824; burial 19 September 1824; “Mortcloth 5/-”. Provider derivative transcript inspected 4 November 2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

This is a possible later record for William, whose November 1747 Covington and Thankerton baptism fits the reported age. If 76 is a completed age on 16 September 1824, it permits a birth between 17 September 1747 and 16 September 1748. The indexed birth year 1748 is calculated from age, rather than supplied by a birth record. No relative, occupation or other detail connects the Hailes Quarry man to the baptised child. The baptism's location and parents therefore remain separate from this adult comparison; neither death nor burial is assigned to William. Other compatible Williams remain possible. The original Colinton entry and a documented adult household or residence link are needed to resolve the identification.
